note: Clans and factions the game depicts or names. `scope` marks how much of each is playable in this game versus held for the sequel.

clans.name: Gu Yue clan
clans.note: The clan controls Moonlight Gu's breeding method, which makes a signature Gu an economic asset as much as a weapon. Its founder is buried under its own history (ch 182-193).

clans.name: Mo family
clans.note: Wealthy within Gu Yue. Its weight is social and financial, which is what makes the extortion arc a political problem rather than a fight.

clans.name: Bai clan
clans.note: Visited as a viewpoint interlude. Bai Ning Bing's grievance against their own clan is the lever Fang Yuan holds.

clans.name: Tie clan
clans.note: Supplies investigators. Tie Xue Leng is named long before Tie Ruo Nan arrives, which is what makes chapter 170 land.

clans.name: Wang family
clans.note: Hunters. The beast-skin map is their working knowledge of the mountain, not a treasure.

clans.name: Chi faction
clans.note: A faction inside Gu Yue. Chi Lian's apparent backing is private leverage presented as long-standing alliance.

clans.name: Yao family
clans.note: Yao Le and Yao Ji. The search for a missing girl is the pressure under the whole of Act IV.

clans.name: Central Continent powers
clans.note: Lord Sky Crane arrives from here, and Fang Zheng is carried toward it. Deliberately left unexplored.

clans.name: Southern Border
clans.note: Where Fang Yuan is heading at chapter 200. Game 2's content package, not this one's.
